newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S. Korean defector recorded video statement - paper.
newsitem.headline: S. Korean defector recorded video statement - paper.

text.p: North Korean Hwang Jang-yop videotaped confirmation of his defection in Seoul's Beijing embassy and this led to a softening of Pyongyang's stand on the issue, a South Korean newspaper said on Thursday.
The daily Joongang Ilbo said South Korean officials passed the tape to the Chinese government which in turn gave it to North Korea. It gave no details of the contents.

Pyongyang had earlier said Hwang was kidnapped but on Monday indicated it was softening its stance over the top ideologue, whose defection marks one of the greatest embarrassments for the Stalinist state.
"Through that videotape, China has learned indirectly that Hwang has indeed defected of his own free will," the newspaper said.

"After analysing the videotape, the Chinese got in touch with the North Koreans and allowed them to look at the tape for themselves. That played a key role in the North Koreans somewhat acknowledging the defection on the 17th (of February)," the daily said.

Hwang arrived at the South Korean embassy in Beijing with an aide on February 12, presenting China with the task of treading a line between North Korea, its traditional ally, and South Korea, a new business partner.
South Korean officials were not available to comment on the newspaper report.
